survivors_flagged.one_line: Sale of China business to Meituan ($717m, up to ~$997m) still pending SAMR clearance and an EGM; the 12-month outside date is ~Feb 2027. After close the shell holds cash and may distribute it. Known since Feb, and no completion news found.

verified.catalyst: SAMR anti-monopoly clearance, an EGM vote and closing of the sale of Dingdong's China business to Meituan's Two Hearts Investments for US$717m cash (up to US$997m total proceeds), after which at least 90% of post-close cash is to be returned through buybacks or dividends.
verified.dated_milestone: The SPA was signed 2026-02-05 and the use-of-proceeds pledge came 2026-02-10. In the Q3 release (2026-11-12) the deal was still pending SAMR. Next hard date: the initial long-stop around 2027-02-05 (extendable by mutual consent). The EGM date is not yet announced.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 named counterparty (Meituan / Two Hearts Investments). G2 concrete commitment (a signed SPA plus a public pledge to return at least 90% of post-close cash). G3 specific figure (US$717m consideration against a ~US$380m market cap, roughly US$3.0-3.9 per ADS distributable on close), which the tape largely does not price.
verified.edge: M. The deal is contractual and the per-ADS gap is large, but the outcome is a binary on Chinese regulators with negative read-across, so it is not mispriced on certainty. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: -46% ($3.20 close on 2026-02-04, before the deal, to $1.74 on 2026-11-20). The stock fell on the announcement and kept falling, so nothing has been harvested. Remaining to the favourable-resolution value: about +84% to roughly $3.20/ADS (range +72% to +124% at $3.0-3.9). The price implies roughly a 20-25% chance of closing against a ~$1.30 break value.
verified.primary_source: Dingdong Q3 2026 results release, 2026-11-12 (deal still pending SAMR). Dingdong use-of-proceeds release, 2026-02-10 (up to US$997m, at least 90% returned). SPA announcement, 2026-02-05. ION/Mergermarket PaRR on SAMR acceptance and rival complaints (2026). FMP quote and EOD prices, 2026-11-20 and 2026-02-04.
verified.analysis: The deal is real, dated and unfired. As of the Q3 release (2026-11-12), the Meituan sale still awaits SAMR, with no EGM date set and the long-stop around Feb 2027. At $1.74 the ADS (market cap about $380m) trades at roughly half the $717m cash consideration, and well below the $3.20 it traded at before the deal was announced. The market is pricing a high chance that SAMR blocks the deal. That is not irrational: Mergermarket/ION reports domestic rivals lodging complaints and senior-government attention, and SAMR held an unusual public hearing on Meituan's separate Maiyatian deal and flagged possible harm to competition. The figures were rebuilt from the deal terms rather than an analyst target: $717m, less an unknown indirect-transfer tax (10% of consideration is held back until taxes are settled), plus a $280m pre-close BVI distribution that is unverified (Q3 cash fell only about $73m, so it may not have been paid), with at least 90% paid out. That gives about $650-850m distributable, or about $3.0-3.9/ADS on roughly 219m ADS. Gaps: the ADS count is derived from market cap, the tax amount is not disclosed, and no 10-Q/20-F capital-structure check was possible within the lookup budget. No preferred stock or external manager is known. This stays WATCH, not ACTIVE, because the event is a coin-flip on regulators with negative read-across, not a mispricing of certainty. Upgrade on SAMR clearance or an EGM notice.
